papers.title: The Conditional Activation Model: Uncovering Policy Demand Responses to AI-Driven Automation
papers.description: Introduces a two-gate framework explaining when citizens update policy preferences in response to AI-driven job automation risk. Pre-registered experiment with 901 U.S. workers; trust-stratum effects recovered by principal-score weighting of both arms.

papers.title: Simulating Open Democracy: An Agent-Based Framework for Testing Deliberative Institutional Designs
papers.description: Open-source simulation using LLM agents as synthetic citizens to test how different institutional rules impact democratic consensus. To be presented at the 2026 MPSA Meeting.

papers.title: One Dimension or Many? The Structure of Artificial Intelligence Attitudes in Mass Publics
papers.description: Maps the structure of U.S. public attitudes toward AI with exploratory factor analysis on a nationally representative sample (N = 5,153): fifty-two items resolve into ten factors organized by the social context of deployment, a belief-system network with no general-attitude hub, and demographic cleavages that reverse direction across dimensions.

papers.citation: Oleg Smirnov, Pei-Hsun Hsieh, & **Ignacio Urbina**. (2025). *Finite pool of worry and emotions in climate change tweets during COVID-19*. *Journal of Environmental Psychology*, 106, 102728. [doi:10.1016/j.jenvp.2025.102728](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jenvp.2025.102728)

papers.title: Fractured Trust: The Spillover Effects of Police Violence on Satisfaction with Democracy and Political Trust
papers.description: Three studies on how exposure to police violence erodes political trust and satisfaction with democracy: a two-wave survey experiment in Brazil (N = 1,004), an observational analysis of Chile's 2019 protest repression, and cross-national LAPOP evidence from sixteen Latin American countries. The damage reaches courts, legislature, and executive rather than stopping at trust in the police.
papers.presentations: Presented at POLMETH (2024), APSA (2024), MPSA (2024), Human Rights Workshop at URI (2024), and others. Winner of Best Poster Award at 2023 Latin American Political Methodology Meeting.

papers.title: Automation Risk, Redistribution, and Economic Vulnerability: Evidence from the European Social Survey, 2002–2022
papers.description: Rebuilds and extends the Thewissen and Rueda (2019) design across all eleven European Social Survey waves (N > 275,000 in 39 countries). The automation risk association with redistribution preferences reappears in 2002–2012 but is smaller in the following decade, with wide country-year variation. Welfare and labor-market institutions condition the exposure–insecurity link: union density weakens it, while net income inequality and strict employment protection strengthen it.

papers.title: Communication and Cooperation with Human and Artificial Agents
papers.description: 2x2 factorial behavioral experiment (oTree): human vs. AI partner, with vs. without communication, in one shot Prisoner's Dilemma and Stag Hunt games.
papers.presentations: Presented at 2023 APSA Meeting, Oxford's Talking to Machines Workshop (2024), and 2024 IMEBESS Conference.

papers.description: Original survey instrument with novel question battery, fielded on Prolific (N ~ 900). Data collection finished.

papers.title: Mind Under Pressure: Does Cognitive Overload Increase Susceptibility to Misinformation?
papers.description: Pre-registered 2x3 factorial survey experiment testing whether an LLM assistant reduces misinformation susceptibility under cognitive overload.

papers.title: Does Trait Aggression Predict Vote Choice for Far-Right Candidates? Evidence from the United States and Brazil
papers.description: Pre-registered cross-national study (US N = 933, Brazil N = 1,004). CFA, logistic regression, mediation analysis. Data collection completed.

papers.authors: Alexa Bankert, Reuben Kline, **Ignacio Urbina**, & Thomas McDonough
papers.title: Minding The (Experimental) Gap(s): Prosociality with Real and Hypothetical Stakes in the Lab and Online
papers.description: Behavioral experiment comparing prosociality with real vs. hypothetical stakes across lab and online settings.

papers.authors: Vitória Sgorlon, **Ignacio Urbina**, Anakiz Elif Senturk, & Santiago Echeverri
papers.title: Misperceptions of Immigrants on the Workforce: Unpacking Labor Market Concerns
papers.description: Four-arm pre-registered experiment (N = 1,810 U.S. workers) testing whether occupation-specific or national facts about immigrants in the workforce reduce perceived economic threat and shift immigration attitudes. Pooled effects are null because over- and under-estimators respond in opposite directions.

papers.title: Bots, Collective Action, and Social Media: An Agent-Based Model of Adversarial Suppression in Polarized Networks
papers.description: Simulates how adversarial bots exploit network topology to suppress political coordination. Bayesian calibration against empirical protest and social media studies.
